decisions.reason: The low-noise burner is a component improvement built directly on the firm's core infrared combustion know-how, so the firm can easily assimilate feedback and refine it across its heater range.

The plaque heater sits squarely in the firm's established gas infrared expertise and had a dedicated page, which signals strategic importance and good capacity to interpret and improve market results.
The luminous radiant heater draws on existing engineering knowledge and the firm's narrow core portfolio, so keeping it consolidates competence rather than wasting resources.
The tube heater builds on long experience in hall heating, though some overlap with Product F slightly raises the chance it is consolidated.
The standard plaque heater was prominently featured and is closely related to the firm's know-how, making it a reliable core offering the firm can maintain and improve.
This second tube heater variant fits the firm's knowledge base well, but its redundancy with Product D makes a portfolio merge somewhat more likely, though a drop is still improbable.
